Question 9 [20 marks]: Compose a piece of imaginative writing that begins with the words:
Some things are unknowable. A person’s secrets may be revealed by the things
they leave behind; but what are they, those supposedly uncovered secrets? They
are words, ideas . . . Dry and dead as dust.
                                                                 © JENNY SINCLAIR, Tamby East
                                           https://www.griffithreview.com/articles/tamby-east/
Note: You are NOT required to write out the extract as part of your response.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Composes a sustained and engaging piece of imaginative writing that skilfully continues the extract | Crafts language skilfully to compose a piece of imaginative writing
13–16 marks: Demonstrates skilful control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and form | Composes a sustained piece of imaginative writing that effectively continues the extract | Crafts language effectively to compose a piece of imaginative writing | Demonstrates effective control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and form
9–12 marks: Composes a sound piece of imaginative writing that continues the extract satisfactorily | Uses language competently to compose a piece of imaginative writing
5–8 marks: Demonstrates sound control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and form | Composes a limited piece of imaginative writing that attempts to continue the extract simply | Uses language variably to compose a piece of imaginative writing | Demonstrates variable control of language and structure

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award.
